input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binds Meridian Fieldworks anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "solicit" (no hits), "induce" (no hits), "recruit", "hire", "no-hire", and "employ" surface only § 12.3 (p0049) plus unrelated references (§ 1.2 employment law, § 18.1 employer's liability insurance) and "personnel" provisions (§§ 1.4, 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) that allocate Vendor's responsibility for its own staff rather than restrict our hiring. § 12.3 goes further in our favour: it preserves our right to hire any person responding to general recruitment — the equivalent of, and broader than, the fallback's general-advertising carve-out — and records that we have made no no-hire commitment. The fallback parameters (12-month duration, general-solicitation and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) are conditions for narrowing a covenant that binds us; because none exists, those deterministic checks are non-probative here and cannot be "fixed" without manufacturing a restriction on ourselves. No redline is proposed, since any edit would be adverse to our client.
